title: Count me in: a youth exchange

task.situation: On the website of the Leafline Youth Network, you have read about ‘Green Cities, Young Voices’, a ten-day youth exchange in Ghent, Belgium, next summer. The exchange is funded by an EU youth programme. Young people aged 15 to 19 from five European countries will work together on ideas for greener towns. You would like to take part and decide to write to the organisers.
points: express your interest and introduce yourself
explain what you could contribute to the exchange
ask about the dates, costs and requirements
task.de: Formelle E-Mail an die Organisator:innen eines erfundenen, von der EU geförderten Jugendaustauschs in Gent. Drei Inhaltspunkte: Interesse zeigen und sich vorstellen; den eigenen Beitrag erklären; nach Terminen, Kosten und Voraussetzungen fragen. Formelles Register, keine Kurzformen.

focus.label: formal phrases for interest and offers
focus.note: Marked: fixed formal email phrases, i.e. greeting and closing formula, purpose statements (I am writing to …, With reference to …), offers (I would be happy to …, I would be glad to …), polite requests and indirect questions (Could you please tell me …, I would also like to know …) and closing sentences (Thank you …, I look forward to …). Linking words and topic introducers are not marked; the subject line is not marked.

gaps.q: How old is our writer? The exchange is for 15- to 19-year-olds.
gaps.qDe: Wie alt ist die Person? Ruft ein Alter zwischen 15 und 17.

gaps.q: Who is writing the email? First name and family name.
gaps.qDe: Ruft einen Vor- und Nachnamen für die Person, die die E-Mail schreibt. Keine Namen von Mitschüler:innen oder Lehrer:innen.

steps.de: Wir entscheiden, an wen die E-Mail geht, und davon hängen Anrede und Grußformel ab.

options.label: The project office (no name)
options.teaser: The website only gives an email address. We do not know who reads the emails.

options.label: The project coordinator, Ms Peeters
options.teaser: The website says: “Any questions? Contact our project coordinator, Ms Anna Peeters.”

steps.q: What do we write in the subject line?
steps.de: Die Betreffzeile sagt in wenigen Wörtern, worum es in der E-Mail geht.
steps.own: Short and specific: what is the email about?
steps.ownDe: Kurz und konkret: Worum geht es in der E-Mail?

options.label: Name the exchange
options.text: Interest in your youth exchange ‘Green Cities, Young Voices’
options.why: The name of the exchange shows the organisers at once what the email is about.

options.label: Name our questions
options.text: Youth exchange in Ghent: questions about dates, costs and requirements
options.why: Tells the reader that the email contains questions and what they are about.

options.label: Who we are
options.text: Enquiry from an Austrian student about your youth exchange
options.why: ‘Enquiry’ is a typical formal word for a subject line, and it says who is writing.

steps.q: How do we greet the reader?
steps.de: Hier wählen wir die Anrede für unsere E-Mail. Prüft jede Option: Aufgabe, Aufbau, Wortschatz, Grammatik.
steps.own: Copy the greeting. Then leave one line free.
steps.ownDe: Anrede abschreiben, danach eine Zeile frei lassen.

options.label: Greeting A
options.why: No name: ‘Dear Sir or Madam’. Name known: ‘Dear Ms’ + surname, never the first name.

options.label: Greeting B
options.reject: This greeting does not suit a formal email in English. ‘Dear Ladies and Gentlemen’ is a word-for-word translation of ‘Sehr geehrte Damen und Herren’: without a name, write ‘Dear Sir or Madam,’. With a name, write ‘Dear Ms Peeters,’ (title and family name only, no first name).
options.rejectDe: Passt nicht zu einer formellen E-Mail: „Dear Ladies and Gentlemen“ ist wörtlich aus „Sehr geehrte Damen und Herren“ übersetzt, richtig ist „Dear Sir or Madam,“; mit Namen „Dear Ms Peeters,“ (Anrede und Nachname, ohne Vornamen).

steps.q: Introduction: how do we start? The purpose comes first!
steps.de: Der erste Absatz nennt den Anlass der E-Mail und stellt uns kurz vor. Prüft jede Option: Aufgabe, Aufbau, Wortschatz, Grammatik.
steps.own: Copy the frame. Then complete the sentences in your own words: name the exchange and say where the writer is from.
steps.ownDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann die Sätze mit eigenen Worten fertigschreiben: den Austausch nennen und sagen, woher die schreibende Person kommt.
steps.ownLong: Copy the frame. Then complete the sentences in your own words: name the exchange, say where the writer is from and add one sentence about what the email will cover or why the exchange is special.
steps.ownLongDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann die Sätze mit eigenen Worten fertigschreiben: den Austausch nennen, sagen, woher die schreibende Person kommt, und einen Satz ergänzen, worum es in der E-Mail geht oder was den Austausch besonders macht.

options.label: Purpose, then who we are
options.text: {{[[I am writing to express my interest in]]}} your youth exchange ‘Green Cities, Young Voices’, which I read about on your website. {{I am a {AGE}-year-old student}} at a grammar school in Linz, Austria, and I would very much like to take part.
options.textLong: {{[[I am writing to express my interest in]]}} your youth exchange ‘Green Cities, Young Voices’, which I read about on your website. {{I am a {AGE}-year-old student}} at a grammar school in Linz, Austria, and I would very much like to take part, as the exchange combines two things I care about: the environment and meeting people from other countries.
options.why: The classic formal opening: the purpose in the very first words, then a short introduction.

options.label: Start with where we found it
options.text: {{[[With reference to]] the information on your website,}} I am very interested in taking part in your youth exchange ‘Green Cities, Young Voices’ in Ghent. {{I am a {AGE}-year-old student}} from Linz, Austria, and I am keen to learn how cities can become greener.
options.textLong: {{[[With reference to]] the information on your website,}} I am very interested in taking part in your youth exchange ‘Green Cities, Young Voices’ in Ghent. {{I am a {AGE}-year-old student}} from Linz, Austria, and I am keen to learn how cities can become greener. I have never taken part in an international project before, so this would be a great opportunity for me.
options.why: ‘With reference to’ is a formal way to refer to an announcement or advert. The purpose follows at once.

steps.q: Body paragraph 1: who are we, and why are we interested?
steps.de: Erster Inhaltspunkt: wer wir sind und warum uns der Austausch interessiert. Prüft jede Option: Aufgabe, Aufbau, Wortschatz, Grammatik.
steps.own: Copy the frame. Then write about the writer’s interests and why the exchange suits them. You can invent the details.
steps.ownDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann über die Interessen der schreibenden Person schreiben und erklären, warum der Austausch zu ihr passt. Details dürfen erfunden sein.
steps.ownLong: Copy the frame. Then write about the writer’s interests and one experience that shows them, and explain why the exchange suits them. You can invent the details.
steps.ownLongDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann über die Interessen der schreibenden Person und ein Erlebnis schreiben, das sie zeigt, und erklären, warum der Austausch zu ihr passt. Details dürfen erfunden sein.

options.label: A school project
options.text: {{My interest in greener cities began at school,}} where my favourite subjects are geography and biology. Last year I helped to set up a school recycling project, and {{since then, environmental topics have become}} more and more important to me. {{That is why}} the idea of working on greener towns with young people from all over Europe appeals to me so much.
options.textLong: {{My interest in greener cities began at school,}} where my favourite subjects are geography and biology. Last year I helped to set up a school recycling project, and {{since then, environmental topics have become}} more and more important to me. Thanks to the project, our school now produces about a third less rubbish. {{However, I have also learnt that}} one school cannot change much on its own. {{That is why}} the idea of working on greener towns with young people from all over Europe appeals to me so much.
options.why: The topic sentence links our interest to the exchange, and a school project shows that it is real.

options.label: Languages and travelling
options.text: {{What attracts me most is the international side of the exchange.}} {{Besides German and English, I speak}} some French. {{Last summer, I travelled}} by train through Slovenia and Croatia with my family. On the way, I met young people from several countries and realised how much we have in common. {{For this reason,}} your exchange is exactly what I am looking for.
options.textLong: {{What attracts me most is the international side of the exchange.}} {{Besides German and English, I speak}} some French and a little Italian. {{Last summer, I travelled}} by train through Slovenia and Croatia with my family. On the way, I met young people from several countries, and although our first languages were different, we soon realised how much we had in common. {{For this reason,}} your exchange is exactly what I am looking for: real teamwork with people of my age.
options.why: The topic sentence names what attracts us, and a short personal experience proves it.

steps.q: Body paragraph 2: what could we contribute?
steps.de: Zweiter Inhaltspunkt: was wir zum Austausch beitragen können. Prüft jede Option: Aufgabe, Aufbau, Wortschatz, Grammatik.
steps.own: Copy the frame. Then describe a skill the writer could offer and how the group could use it.
steps.ownDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann eine Fähigkeit der schreibenden Person beschreiben und erklären, wie die Gruppe davon profitieren könnte.
steps.ownLong: Copy the frame. Then describe a skill the writer could offer, how the group could use it and what it would bring.
steps.ownLongDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann eine Fähigkeit der schreibenden Person beschreiben, wie die Gruppe sie nutzen könnte und was sie bringen würde.

options.label: Photos and videos
options.text: {{If I am given a place, [[I would be glad to]]}} document the exchange. I take photos for our school magazine and know how to edit short videos, so I could make a video diary of our time in Ghent. {{It would give the other participants something to show}} when they present the project at their own schools.
options.textLong: {{If I am given a place, [[I would be glad to]]}} document the exchange. I take photos for our school magazine and know how to edit short videos, so I could make a video diary of our time in Ghent. Each evening, I could put together a short clip about the day’s work. {{It would give the other participants something to show}} when they present the project at their own schools, and it might encourage others to apply.
options.why: The topic sentence links our offer to taking part, and the paragraph explains how the group could profit.

options.label: A taste of Austria
options.text: {{In return for this chance, [[I would be happy to]] help organise}} an intercultural evening. Together with other Austrian participants, I could present a few typical dishes, including Kaiserschmarrn, and teach the group a simple card game from Austria. {{Moreover, I play the guitar,}} so music could be part of the evening as well.
options.textLong: {{In return for this chance, [[I would be happy to]] help organise}} an intercultural evening. Together with other Austrian participants, I could present a few typical dishes, including Kaiserschmarrn, and teach the group a simple card game from Austria. Participants from the other countries could do the same, and everyone would learn something new about their neighbours. {{Moreover, I play the guitar,}} so music could be part of the evening as well. Evenings like this often help a group to grow together.
options.why: The topic sentence links back to the chance we hope for. ‘Moreover’ adds a second thing we could offer.

options.label: Photos, videos and music
options.text: I can help the group in a lot of ways, and I can take photos, and I can make short videos, and then I can show them to everybody at the end, and I can also help with an Austrian evening, and I can cook something, and I can play the guitar, so I can do a lot for the exchange.
options.textLong: I can help the group in a lot of ways, and I can take photos, and I can make short videos, and then I can show them to everybody at the end, and I can also help with an Austrian evening, and I can cook something typical, and I can teach the others a card game, and I can play the guitar, so I can do a lot of things for the exchange and for the group.
options.reject: One endless sentence: idea after idea glued together with ‘and’. Split it into sentences and use formal phrases for offers (I would be glad to …, I would be happy to …, Moreover, …).
options.rejectDe: Ein einziger endloser Satz: Ein Gedanke nach dem anderen wird mit „and“ angehängt. In Sätze teilen und formelle Wendungen für Angebote verwenden (I would be glad to …, I would be happy to …, Moreover …).

steps.q: Body paragraph 3: what do we ask about dates, costs and requirements?
steps.de: Dritter Inhaltspunkt: unsere Fragen zu Terminen, Kosten und Voraussetzungen. Prüft jede Option: Aufgabe, Aufbau, Wortschatz, Grammatik.
steps.own: Copy the frame. Then write your own polite questions about the dates, costs and requirements.
steps.ownDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann eigene höfliche Fragen zu Terminen, Kosten und Voraussetzungen formulieren.
steps.ownLong: Copy the frame. Then write your own polite questions about the dates, costs and requirements, and give a reason for one of them.
steps.ownLongDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann eigene höfliche Fragen zu Terminen, Kosten und Voraussetzungen formulieren und eine davon begründen.

options.label: Straight to the questions
options.text: Finally, I have some questions about the practical details. When exactly does the exchange take place, and could you send me some informations about the costs of the trip to Ghent? I would also like to know whether I have to send my application until the end of March. Will we stay with host families? Do I need a certain level of English, or is it enough when I can communicate well?
options.textLong: Finally, I have some questions about the practical details. When exactly does the exchange take place, and could you send me some informations about the costs of the trip to Ghent? I would also like to know whether I have to send my application until the end of March and whether I need a letter from my school. Will we stay with host families or in a youth hostel? Do I need a certain level of English, or is it enough when I can communicate well?
options.reject: Three typical mistakes: ‘informations’ (→ information, no plural), ‘send my application until the end of March’ (→ by the end of March: a deadline) and ‘enough when’ (→ enough if).
options.rejectDe: Drei typische Fehler: information hat keinen Plural, bei einer Frist heißt „bis“ by (nicht until), enough when → enough if (Bedingung).

options.label: One question after the other
options.text: {{Before I apply, I have a few questions.}} {{[[Could you please tell me]]}} the exact dates and the deadline for applications? {{[[I would also like to know]] whether}} travel costs are covered by the programme or whether participants pay a fee. {{Lastly, [[I would be interested to know]] whether}} there are any requirements, such as a minimum level of English or parental consent.
options.textLong: {{Before I apply, I have a few questions.}} {{[[Could you please tell me]]}} the exact dates and the deadline for applications? {{[[I would also like to know]] whether}} travel costs are covered by the programme or whether participants pay a fee. As the journey from Linz takes most of a day, [[it would be useful to know]] whether you book the train tickets for the participants. {{Lastly, [[I would be interested to know]] whether}} there are any requirements, such as a minimum level of English or parental consent.
options.why: Dates, costs and requirements in a clear order, each with a polite formal phrase.

options.label: Practical details
options.text: {{When it comes to the practical details, [[I would be grateful if you could tell me]]}} when exactly the exchange starts and ends. {{[[It would also be helpful to know]]}} how much participants have to pay themselves and which costs are covered by the programme. {{Furthermore, [[please let me know]] if}} there are any requirements, such as a language test.
options.textLong: {{When it comes to the practical details, [[I would be grateful if you could tell me]]}} when exactly the exchange starts and ends. As I have a summer job in August, the dates matter to me. {{[[It would also be helpful to know]]}} how much participants have to pay themselves and which costs are covered by the programme, for example travel and food. {{Furthermore, [[please let me know]] if}} there are any requirements, such as a language test or a letter from my school.
options.why: Three indirect questions with three different formal phrases. No question word order inside them.

steps.q: Conclusion: how do we end the email?
steps.de: Der Schluss greift unser Anliegen auf und rundet die E-Mail ab. Prüft jede Option: Aufgabe, Aufbau, Wortschatz, Grammatik.
steps.own: Copy the frame. Then add one sentence of your own that links back to the writer’s wish to take part.
steps.ownDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann in einem eigenen Satz auf den Wunsch der schreibenden Person zurückverweisen, am Austausch teilzunehmen.
steps.ownLong: Copy the frame. Then add one or two sentences of your own that link back to the writer’s wish to take part.
steps.ownLongDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann in ein bis zwei eigenen Sätzen auf den Wunsch der schreibenden Person zurückverweisen, am Austausch teilzunehmen.

options.label: Our wish and a reason to reply soon
options.text: {{[[Thank you in advance for]]}} your answers. I would love to bring my ideas to Ghent, and since I need to talk to my parents and my school first, {{[[I would appreciate an early reply.]]}}
options.textLong: {{[[Thank you in advance for]]}} your answers. Taking part would mean a lot to me, and I would love to bring my ideas to Ghent. Since I need to talk to my parents and my school first, {{[[I would appreciate an early reply.]]}}
options.why: It picks up our wish to take part and gives a good reason for a quick reply.

options.label: Thanks and a final detail
options.text: Thank you for your help. I would also like to know whether my best friend could come too, even though she is only fourteen, and whether there is Wi-Fi where we will stay. I look forward to hearing from you.
options.textLong: Thank you for reading my email and for your help. I would also like to know whether my best friend could come too, even though she is only fourteen. She is also very interested in the environment. Another question is whether there is Wi-Fi where we will stay. I look forward to hearing from you.
options.reject: New questions do not belong in the conclusion. The conclusion only thanks the reader and asks for a reply; all questions go into the paragraph before.
options.rejectDe: Neue Fragen gehören nicht in den Schluss. Der Schluss bedankt sich nur und bittet um eine Antwort.

options.label: Thanks and an offer to talk
options.text: {{[[Thank you for reading my email.]]}} I very much hope to join the exchange, and {{[[I would be pleased to]]}} tell you more about myself in a phone call. {{[[I look forward to hearing from you]]}} soon.
options.textLong: {{[[Thank you for reading my email.]]}} I very much hope to join the exchange and to take new ideas back to Linz. {{If it helps your decision, [[I would be pleased to]]}} tell you more about myself in a phone or video call. {{[[I look forward to hearing from you]]}} soon.
options.why: It picks up our wish to join, offers a phone or video call and ends with the classic last line.

steps.de: Am Ende stehen die Grußformel und darunter der volle Name, den ihr gleich selbst bestimmt. Prüft jede Option: Aufgabe, Aufbau, Wortschatz, Grammatik.
steps.own: Copy the closing formula and, on the next line, the full name we chose.
steps.ownDe: Grußformel abschreiben, darunter den gewählten vollen Namen.

options.label: Sign-off A
options.reject: ‘Kind regards’ is for emails to people we already know. A formal email to someone we have never met ends with ‘Yours faithfully’ (after ‘Dear Sir or Madam’) or ‘Yours sincerely’ (after ‘Dear Ms Peeters’).
options.rejectDe: „Kind regards“ passt zu E-Mails an Bekannte. Formell: „Yours faithfully“ nach „Dear Sir or Madam“, „Yours sincerely“ nach „Dear Ms Peeters“.

options.label: Sign-off B
options.why: ‘Dear Sir or Madam’ goes with ‘Yours faithfully’, ‘Dear Ms Peeters’ with ‘Yours sincerely’. Then our full name.

checks.en: A subject line that says clearly what the email is about
Greeting and closing match: Dear Sir or Madam → Yours faithfully, Dear Ms … → Yours sincerely
The first sentence says why we are writing
All three content points: interest and introduction, our contribution, questions about dates, costs and requirements
Five paragraphs: introduction, one paragraph per content point, conclusion; no new questions in the conclusion
Formal register: no contractions, no slang, polite indirect questions
The conclusion picks up our wish to take part and asks for a reply; our full name comes at the end

teacher.aim: Die Klasse baut gemeinsam eine formelle E-Mail (B1) an die Organisator:innen eines von der EU geförderten Jugendaustauschs und übt dabei die Konventionen der formellen E-Mail: Betreff, passende Anrede und Grußformel, Zweck im ersten Satz, ein Punkt pro Absatz, höfliche indirekte Fragen, kein Slang und keine Kurzformen.
teacher.prep: A/B/C/D-Karten austeilen, Beamer im Vollbild. An der Tafel eine kleine Tabelle vorbereiten: „Dear Sir or Madam → Yours faithfully“ und „Dear Ms … → Yours sincerely“. Nach Schritt 1 markieren, welche Zeile für unsere E-Mail gilt. Im Gerüst-Modus den eingebauten Timer nutzen: 5 min pro Absatz (lange Fassung: 7–8 min), bei Bedarf +1. Hefte bereitlegen. Die Aufgabe am Beamer enthält alles Nötige.
teacher.heft: Neue Seite: Datum (rechts) und „Email“ als Überschrift (wie am Beamer). Darunter der E-Mail-Kopf mit vier Zeilen (To, From, Date, Subject) wie am Beamer; der Betreff kommt nach der zweiten Entscheidung in die Subject-Zeile, der Name erst unter die Grußformel. Anrede in einer eigenen Zeile, dann eine Zeile frei. Jeder Absatz beginnt nach einer Leerzeile, am Rand steht das Randwort (Intro, Body 1, Body 2, Body 3, Conclusion). Vor der Grußformel eine Zeile frei, dann Grußformel und Name in zwei eigenen Zeilen. Formelle Wendungen (Interesse, Angebote, Bitten, Schluss) grün unterstreichen.
teacher.flow: Volltext kurz (50 min): 5 min Aufgabe lesen, 9 Entscheidungen (Empfänger:in, Betreff, Anrede und Grußformel gehen schnell, ca. 1 min; die fünf Absätze ca. 2 min), Abschreiben ca. 20 min, 5 min Checkliste. Volltext lang (Doppelstunde): dieselben 9 Entscheidungen, aber längere Absätze (Einleitung ca. 55 Wörter, Body 1 bis 3 je ca. 80, Schluss ca. 50); Abschreiben ca. 30 min, zusammen ca. 60 min. Die restliche Zeit für die Besprechung der Fallen und den Beginn der Hausübung nutzen. Gerüst kurz (geplant 60 min): 5 min Aufgabe; Empfänger:in, Betreff, Anrede und Grußformel je ca. 1 min; pro Absatz 1 min Entscheidung, realistisch 5–6 min eigenes Schreiben, 1 min Vergleich mit dem Modell. In 50 min: beim Schluss nur abstimmen und das Gerüst abschreiben, den eigenen Satz und die Checkliste als Hausübung. Gerüst lang (Doppelstunde, 100 min): dieselben Entscheidungen; für Body 1 bis 3 je ca. 8 min eigenes Schreiben, für Einleitung und Schluss je ca. 5 min, dazu je 1 min Entscheidung und 1 min Vergleich; am Ende 5 min Checkliste.
teacher.traps: Greeting B (TA): „Dear Ladies and Gentlemen,“ (wörtlich aus „Sehr geehrte Damen und Herren“) bzw. „Dear Ms Anna Peeters,“ (nach Ms nur der Nachname). Body 2 C (LSR): ein einziger endloser Satz, in dem ein Gedanke nach dem anderen mit „and“ angehängt wird, statt formeller Angebote. Body 3 A (LSA): informations (kein Plural), until the end of March statt by (Frist), enough when statt enough if. Conclusion B (CC): neue Fragen im Schluss. Sign-off A (TA): „Kind regards“ passt nur zu E-Mails an Bekannte, formell „Yours faithfully“ bzw. „Yours sincerely“. Kürzel: TA = Erfüllung der Aufgabenstellung, CC = Kohärenz und Kohäsion, LSR = Spektrum sprachlicher Mittel, LSA = Sprachrichtigkeit.
teacher.notes: Jede Fassung hat fünf Absätze (Einleitung, drei Hauptabsätze, Schluss). Die lange Fassung hat dieselben Entscheidungen, alle fünf Absätze sind darin etwas länger; sie fügt keinen Absatz hinzu. Bei „Greeting“ und „Sign-off“ gibt es nur eine richtige Option: Die eigentliche Entscheidung (Name bekannt oder nicht) fällt in Schritt 1, hier geht es nur um die Falle. Austausch, Netzwerk, Kontaktperson und Adressen sind erfunden; das EU-Förderprogramm bleibt bewusst ohne Namen. Für den Namen in der Grußformel nur erfundene Namen, keine Namen von Mitschüler:innen oder Lehrer:innen. Differenzierung: Schnelle ergänzen im Gerüst-Modus eine zusätzliche Frage, z. B. zur Unterkunft. Hausübung: zweite Fassung an die andere Empfängerin bzw. das Büro, mit angepasster Anrede und Grußformel und zwei anderen Entscheidungen.
